order_tables.title: Approved Truing Up of account for the year 2020-21

power_purchase.kserc_reasoning: The 2/3rd of efficiency gain at average power purchase cost of Rs 2.31 lakh is hereby allowed to the power purchase cost and the Commission hereby approves the power purchase cost of Rs.3169.77 lakh for the purpose of truing-up for the year 2020-21.
key_observations: Difference in power purchase cost with KSEB Ltd records (Rs. 3167.46 lakh claimed vs Rs. 3176.65 lakh as per KSEBL records).
Efficiency gain due to lower actual distribution loss (1.27%) compared to approved (1.38%).
power_purchase.methodology_applied: Regulation 72 (4) of Tariff Regulations 2018 (sharing of efficiency gain 2:1 between licensee and consumers).

employee_cost.kserc_reasoning: Since the actual employee cost is within the norms fixed, the Commission hereby approves the actual employee expenses of Rs.137.93 lakh for the year 2020-21.
key_observations: Licensee limited employee cost to a level lower than the norms fixed by the Commission.
Overall employee cost decreased from Rs.138.96 lakh in 2019-20 to Rs.137.93 lakh in 2020-21.
employee_cost.methodology_applied: Approved as per actuals, as it was within norms.

repair_maintenance.kserc_reasoning: The Commission has duly considered the explanations/clarifications furnished in the licensee's submission regarding the emergency/one time works undertaken in 2020-21 to provide reliable supply to consumers. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the actual amount of Rs.8.95 lakh as R&M expense for the year 2020-21.
key_observations: Increase of Rs.3.75 lakhs (72.12%) in R&M expense compared to 2019-20.
Reasons for increase include works postponed from FY 2019-20 due to COVID-19 and emergency/one-time works undertaken in 2020-21.
repair_maintenance.methodology_applied: Approved as per actuals, considering explanations for increase.

admin_general.kserc_reasoning: Considering the details furnished by the licensee and decision of the licensee to revamp the entire prepaid metering system to new prepaid smart energy meter system and associated software by December 2023, the Commission hereby approves the actual amount of Rs.35.69 lakh as the Administrative and General expenses for the year 2020-21.
key_observations: Total A&G expense increased by 20.05% compared to the previous year.
Increase mainly due to the increase in monthly charge for management of prepaid metering system (from Rs.0.55 lakh to Rs.1.32 lakh).
Licensee is planning to revamp the entire prepaid metering system to new prepaid smart energy meter system by December 2023.
admin_general.methodology_applied: Approved as per actuals, considering explanations and future plans for system revamp.

depreciation.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, against a claim of Rs.96.47 lakh in the Truing Up petition, the Commission hereby approves the depreciation of Rs.36.65 lakh for the year 2020-21.
key_observations: Licensee claimed depreciation for the entire assets, though not eligible for depreciation on assets created out of accumulated regulatory surplus.
Assets worth Rs.948.39 lakh were created out of accumulated surplus, and depreciation of Rs.48.91 lakh applicable to these assets is deducted.
depreciation.methodology_applied: Regulation 27(2) (depreciation on fixed assets), disallowance of depreciation on assets created from accumulated regulatory surplus.

interest_long_term.kserc_reasoning: The licensee has not claimed any interest and finance charges for 2020-21.

interest_consumer_deposits.kserc_reasoning: Since the licensee is following the pre-payment metering system, interest on working capital is also not allowable.
interest_consumer_deposits.methodology_applied: Disallowed as per pre-payment metering system.

return_on_nfa.kserc_reasoning: As shown above, after deducting the assets created out of accumulated surplus, the RoNFA eligible for the year 2020-21 is Rs. 15.73 lakh. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves Rs.15.73 lakh (3% of Rs.524.17 lakh) as return on net fixed assets for the year 2020-21 as against Rs.34.85 lakh claimed by the licensee.
key_observations: Assets created from 2016-17 using accumulated surplus have no cost of funds.
Return on NFA is not allowable for assets created from accumulated surplus.
return_on_nfa.methodology_applied: Deduction of RoNFA on assets created from accumulated regulatory surplus.

energy_decision.kserc_reasoning: The Commission hereby approves the actual distribution loss of 1.27% as claimed by the licensee. Accordingly, as per the provision of the regulations, the power purchase cost for the year is computed as shown below.
energy_decision.excess_demand_action: No excess demand or charges were recorded for 2020-21 as per Table 4.

capital_structure_verified.kserc_reasoning: The Commission after considering the items of capital expenditure of Rs.341.72 lakh and the submissions by the petitioner to justify this expenditure, approves Rs.341.72 lakh for inclusion in the asset base, subject to the condition that the licensee is not eligible for depreciation and other financing costs on the said items. It is pertinent to mention that assets worth Rs.948.39 lakh are created out of the accumulated surplus till the year 2020-21 as per the approved figures.
